author: Great Lakes Wire
title: Grass identification course to be held at W.K. Kellogg Biological Station in July
text:
Michigan State University Extension announced on May 27 that a two-day grass identification course will be held at the W.K. Kellogg Biological Station from July 30-31. The course aims to help participants understand the unique anatomy of grasses and provide insights into ecological principles that assist with accurate plant identification.
The program is designed for conservation professionals, resource managers, amateurs interested in plant diversity, and anyone curious about grasses. Participants will receive expert instruction, participate in fieldwork and lab sessions, and learn about grass morphology, terminology, species found in southern Michigan, and the ecological roles of grasses across various habitats.
The workshop will be led by Tyler Bassett, Ph.D., co-lead botanist with the Michigan Natural Features Inventory through Michigan State University Extension, and Brad Slaughter, senior botanist with Orbis Environmental Consulting. According to the announcement, “Tyler has over 25 years of experience studying the ecology, classification and management of ecosystems… Brad is a botanist and vegetation ecologist with nearly 20 years of experience managing and conducting projects.” The cost for participation is $250 for Sanctuary members or $300 for non-members; registration includes a copy of “Grasses of the Northern Forest: A Photographic Guide.” Registration closes on July 27 or when capacity reaches 20 participants.
Registration details are available through the W.K. Kellogg Biological Station Community Relations Office at communityrelations@kbs.msu.edu.
The College of Agriculture and Natural Resources at Michigan State University addresses challenges in food, health, and environmental sustainability through education and outreach programs. It operates research centers across Michigan via MSU Extension services while collaborating through major research centers involving more than 340 scientists. In fall 2021, it reported an enrollment of 3,735 students as part of its mission to foster a healthy world through student preparation and sustainable agriculture practices, according to the official website .
